body.estimand_functional: \(\theta_G=F_G(\operatorname{vech}\Sigma)\), with minimum recursive certificate degree \(ID_G\) and graph-uniform frontier \(D_2(n)\)

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from a fixed acyclic linear Gaussian structural equation model.
sampling_model.units: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent copies of the observed \(n\)-vector.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the full supported structural mechanism.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; regularity is stated through covariance, rational-denominator, and influence-covariance margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(\Sigma\) by \(\widehat\Sigma\), differentiate the deterministic rational output \(F_G\), and estimate the joint influence covariance by empirical plug-in averaging. At a sample denominator pole use the zero evaluation convention; at a pole or singular \(\widehat V_F\), return \(\mathbb R^r\) as the confidence set.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For prespecified \(d\ge ID_G\), the degree-bounded algorithm returns minimum-degree formulas; Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 bound half-trek and instrumental-cutset certificates by \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 bounds auxiliary-cutset certificates by \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\), yielding \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\).
The half-trek criterion is a polynomial-time sufficient criterion for rational identification by recursive linear systems.
Instrumental cutsets give a sound graphical identification criterion for linear structural causal models.
Auxiliary cutsets enlarge the efficiently certifiable subclass by recursively using identified coefficients as auxiliary information.
A missing cycle in a directed-tree model yields a quadratic equation, and multiple cycles can select one rational root.
Every directed-tree structural coefficient is generically one-identifiable, two-identifiable, or unidentifiable, and the classification is complete.
The complete tree-only identification predicate can be implemented in randomized \(O(n^3\log^2n)\) time.
A Cohen--Macaulay graph or Rees algebra yields inverse-degree bounds through regularity and Jacobian-dual minors.
Generic identification in unrestricted linear structural causal models has a sound and complete polynomial-space decision procedure.
Fixed half-trek estimators have recursive influence functions, asymptotic normality, and plug-in Wald inference.
Bow-free path recovery is stable under quantitative conditions, while a four-node example has unbounded condition number.
At a vanishing constraint gradient, the Wald statistic can converge to a nonstandard rational function of a Gaussian vector.

body.tldr: The field-level target is the sharp recursive degree frontier \(D_2(n)\) over every structural and disturbance coordinate and every identifying order. The lower program starts from the explicit two-parent windmills, requires an audited \(W_3^{(2)}\) instance with rational formulas, exhaustive half-trek, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset failure transcripts, and exact degree-four rank-obstruction matrices for every reachable predecessor set, and then lifts the substitution-robust obstruction to the family; the upper program matches that scale through the multigraded covariance-map algebra. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give the bound \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\); the resulting \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) bounds at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\) are cited background. Only after the uniform frontier is proved is it compiled into a total formula-returning schedule; its fixed rational output is evaluated with an explicit pole convention and yields a Wald set that is the full parameter space on pole or singular covariance events, which vanish uniformly on regular charts.

project_justification.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's algorithm is complete only relative to a supplied degree. Their Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) for the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses, and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) for auxiliary cutsets, specializing to \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\). No theorem calibrates minimum recursive degree over all rationally identifiable indegree-two graphs or exhibits an explicit family outside auxiliary cutsets with an order-robust lower invariant.
project_justification.niche: Directed indegree two is the first sparse class in which a missing covariance equation can couple four structural coefficients. The explicit windmill family isolates this block interaction while retaining an exact rank-intersection filtration that includes disturbance-coordinate shortcuts.
project_justification.fill: The central open-ended question proves matching bounds for \(D_2(n)\), establishes the padded two-parent windmills as a rationally identifiable family outside all three bounded graphical subclasses, and lower-bounds them with \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\) over every degree-reachable predecessor set. The mandatory \(W_3^{(2)}\) audit supplies coordinate formulas, three complete criterion-failure transcripts, and every degree-four obstruction matrix before the family induction. The resulting cutoff is compiled conditionally into exact formula output and total finite-sample fixed-chart inference.

body.related_work: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma define \(ID_G\), return minimum-degree rational formulas below a prespecified cutoff, and identify structural degree growth as the missing complexity input. Their Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give the half-trek and instrumental-cutset bounds \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), while Proposition 7.4 gives the auxiliary-cutset bound \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\); at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\), these are \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\). These results are cited background. The sharp-frontier question strictly tightens their prespecified-degree guarantee only on the full rationally identifiable indegree-two class. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton supply the half-trek linear-system baseline. Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim introduce instrumental cutsets, while Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim introduce auxiliary cutsets; the worked \(W_3^{(2)}\) instance and the full windmill family require exhaustive failure transcripts for all three criteria. Van der Zander et al. derive the bilinear missing-cycle equations, while Gupta and Bläser prove the complete tree-only one, two, or infinite classification and Briefs and Bläser accelerate that predicate; these papers inform the degree-four kill test rather than serve as frontier targets. Hassanzadeh and Simis motivate Hilbert control of birational inverse degree, but their hypotheses are not assumed for SEM covariance maps. Dörfler et al. provide the total decision benchmark without formula output. Mareis, Sturma, and Drton inform fixed-chart inference for deterministic rational output; Sankararaman, Louis, and Goyal motivate quantitative conditioning, and Drton and Xiao delimit the singular Wald boundary. The finite-sample construction therefore assigns the full ambient parameter space at denominator poles or singular plug-in covariance matrices and proves both exceptional events vanish uniformly on the fixed chart.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The six-vertex two-triangle construction supplies only a rational certificate of degree at most nine and does not establish \(ID_{K_6}>4\). The two-parent windmills are explicit candidate gadgets, but even the required \(W_3^{(2)}\) formulas, three criterion-failure transcripts, and degree-four rank-obstruction matrices are open deliverables rather than presolved facts. The upper Hilbert comparison must be proved for the SEM recursive filtration; no Cohen--Macaulay property or equality with projective inverse degree is assumed.
body.honest_scope: The field-level contribution is the open-ended two-sided frontier together with its explicit outside-auxiliary-cutset windmill family and substitution-robust Hilbert-rank lower invariant. The closure equivalence, three-vertex census, exact \(W_3^{(2)}\) audit, windmill separation, matching scale, and fixed-chart inferential extension are claims to prove. The degree-four computation is a falsification gate. The total stopping schedule is explicitly conditional on a proved uniform frontier and has no unconditional force before that result. The inference theorem is fixed-dimensional and regular-chart; its estimator is set to zero at a sample denominator pole, its Wald set is the full ambient space at a pole or singular \(\widehat V_F\), and both exceptional events must vanish uniformly. No semiparametric efficiency, adaptive formula-selection validity, growing-dimension Gaussian approximation, or singular-chart coverage is claimed. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\), hence \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\); the exact base case is \(D_2(3)=3\).
